questions.prompt: A particle has displacement \(30\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(5\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its average velocity.
A particle moves from \(12\,\mathrm{m}\) to \(-8\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(4\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its average velocity.
Why is average speed always greater than or equal to the magnitude of average velocity?
questions.answer:
Distance traveled is always greater than or equal to displacement magnitude:
\[
d\geq |\Delta x|
\]
Dividing by the same positive \(\Delta t\) gives the result.

questions.prompt: A runner travels \(100\,\mathrm{m}\) out and \(100\,\mathrm{m}\) back in \(20\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average velocity and average speed.
For \(x(t)=3t+2\), find the average velocity from \(t=1\,\mathrm{s}\) to \(t=5\,\mathrm{s}\).
A particle is at \(0\,\mathrm{m}\) when \(t=2\,\mathrm{s}\) and \(18\,\mathrm{m}\) when \(t=8\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average velocity.
A particle moves \(+10\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(2\,\mathrm{s}\), then \(-4\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(3\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average velocity and average speed.
What are the SI units of average velocity?
questions.answer:
Average velocity is displacement divided by time:
\[
\bar{v}_x=\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}
\]
So the SI unit is \(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

questions.prompt: A particle moves at \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for \(2\,\mathrm{s}\), then \(-2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for \(6\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the average velocity.
If a particle has zero average velocity over a nonzero time interval, what must be true about its initial and final positions?
questions.answer:
The displacement must be zero:
\[
\bar{v}_x=0\Rightarrow \Delta x=0
\]
So \(x_f=x_i\).

questions.prompt: A car moves from \(x=-50\,\mathrm{m}\) to \(x=10\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(15\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its average velocity.
Can average velocity be negative while average speed is positive?
questions.answer: Yes. Average velocity uses displacement, so it carries direction. Average speed uses distance, so it cannot be negative.

questions.prompt: During a \(10\,\mathrm{s}\) interval, a particle travels \(60\,\mathrm{m}\) of distance but has displacement \(-20\,\mathrm{m}\). Find average velocity and average speed.
A position table gives \(x=1\,\mathrm{m}\) at \(t=0\,\mathrm{s}\) and \(x=19\,\mathrm{m}\) at \(t=6\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the average velocity.
A particle has \(\bar{v}_x=-3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for \(8\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its displacement.
A particle starts at \(5\,\mathrm{m}\) and has average velocity \(2.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for \(4\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its final position.
Why is average velocity undefined for \(\Delta t=0\)?
questions.answer:
The definition would require division by zero:
\[
\bar{v}_x=\frac{\Delta x}{0}
\]
So the time interval must be nonzero.

questions.prompt: A particle moves \(8\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(2\,\mathrm{s}\), then \(8\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(6\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its average velocity for the whole motion.
On a position-time graph, what does average velocity represent between two points?
questions.answer:
It is the slope of the secant line:
\[
\bar{v}_x=\frac{x_f-x_i}{t_f-t_i}
\]

questions.prompt: A particle has average velocity \(7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) for \(3\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its displacement.

A particle moves from \(x=0\) to \(x=12\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(3\,\mathrm{s}\), then from \(x=12\,\mathrm{m}\) to \(x=-4\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(5\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average velocity and average speed over the whole motion.
A particle has \(x(t)=t^2-6t+5\). Find the average velocity from \(t=1\,\mathrm{s}\) to \(t=7\,\mathrm{s}\), and decide whether it equals the instantaneous velocity at the midpoint time.
